newsitem.title: USA: Poll shows Clinton with biggest Pennsylvania lead.
newsitem.headline: Poll shows Clinton with biggest Pennsylvania lead.

text.p: President Clinton held his biggest lead yet over Republican challenger Bob Dole in Pennsylvania, according to a statewide poll published Wednesday.

Clinton held a 16-point, 49-33 percent lead over Dole in the Philadelphia Daily News/KYW Keystone poll of 626 registered voters surveyed Sunday through Monday. Clinton's lead has grown from 14 points in March and 11 in August.
Reform Party candidate Ross Perot was a distant third, at 6 percent in the latest poll, down 10 points from his high in March and 4 points from August.

The poll showed Dole with only 60 percent support among the state's Republicans, while Clinton had 72 percent support among the Democrats, who outnumber Republicans in the state. Pennsylvania traditionally is a swing state in presidential elections.
Clinton won Pennsylvania in 1992, but the Democrats lost a Senate seat in the state two years later.

Dole was to campaign Wednesday in heavily Republican central Pennsylvania. In April, Dole had identified Pennsylvania as a crucial state to his campaign, saying if he won the state and its 23 electoral votes, he would win the presidency.
